## CPython 3.13 Free Threading and Extension Imports

CPython 3.13 introduced free threading as an experimental configuration in which the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) can be disabled. In this mode, what happens at an extension’s import boundary depends in part on whether the extension explicitly declares support for free threading.

If an extension has no such declaration, importing it produces a warning and enables the GIL. The way to make the declaration differs between extensions that use multi-phase initialization and those that use single-phase initialization.

Declaring support signals compatibility with the free-threading runtime mode. It is separate from making the extension’s code thread-safe: the declaration alone does not do that.
